## What was tried

Part 3 of the v5.0.0 impact validation (#354) measured one codegraph first-index build at a time. A session-start hook builds an index for every new git checkout (every clone and every worktree) that has no `.codegraph/codegraph.db`. The hook has no lock and no limit on how many builds run at once. Several agent worktrees opened together in one workspace run several builds together. Nobody has measured that.

**William's single-build results (2026-11-17, #354 comment https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/354#issuecomment-6955365431).** Fresh shallow clones, sequential, codegraph 1.6.2. Limits: peak memory at most 1,048,576 KiB, index at most 140 KiB per indexed file.

| Project | Init time | Peak memory (KiB) | Indexed files | KiB per file | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PrivateProjectA | 15.551 s | 1,472,456 | 1,063 | 62.81 | FAIL: memory |
| PrivateProjectB | 1.019 s | 484,332 | 37 | 43.57 | PASS |
| EndlessRunnerSampleGame | 2.820 s | 460,776 | 101 | 57.90 | PASS |

**Claude's quick check (2026-11-18, not a full measurement).** IronClaude master (`3f3b34a2`, 33,697 tracked files) copied once per build, on a shared Coder workspace with about 23 GiB of memory available. One run per level, not repeated. The run was stopped on Clay's instruction before 5 and 10 builds.

| Builds at the same time | Per-build peak (KiB) | Sum of peaks | Available-memory drop | Wall time |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3,720,212 | 3,720,212 KiB (3.5 GiB) | 3,326,192 KiB | 44 s |
| 3 | 3,693,536; 3,768,368; 3,718,280 | 11,180,184 KiB (10.7 GiB) | 11,298,544 KiB | 63 s |

The one-build IronClaude index had 3,430 indexed files, 46,776 nodes, a 160 MB database. Peak memory appears to grow with the number of indexed files. A single IronClaude build peaks at 3.5 times the limit that PrivateProjectA failed.

Each person has their own Coder workspace, so memory from different people does not add up. Only concurrent worktrees in one workspace do. The hook and its documented cost: `src/superclaude/hooks/scripts/codegraph-session-start.sh`; `docs/user-guide/codegraph.md` lines 23 to 30 ("about 70 KB of disk per indexed file and up to about 1 GB of memory during the first init"). The off switch is `SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_AUTOINIT=0`.

## Relevant files and links

- Parent: #354 (runbook row RB8, "codegraph auto-index hook cost"). William's single-build comment is linked above.
- Hook script: `src/superclaude/hooks/scripts/codegraph-session-start.sh`. Docs: `docs/user-guide/codegraph.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` line 332.
- Method used for the single builds: `docs/testing/v5.0.0/impact-validation/william.md` lines 88 to 104.
- Claude's quick-check script and raw results are in `/tmp/cgtest/` on the coordinator workspace (`run.py`, `results.json`, `out.log`). They are temporary.

## Done when

1. On one workspace, for N = 1, 3, 5 and 10 fresh shallow clones of the same repository started at the same moment, the comment on this issue reports each build's peak memory, each build's wall time, the sum of the peaks, and the lowest available memory (`MemAvailable` in `/proc/meminfo`, sampled every second or faster).
2. The same is done for PrivateProjectA and for the IronClaude repository itself.
3. Any build that failed, was killed, or made the machine slow is reported, with the workspace's total memory.
4. The result is posted as one comment on this issue and linked on #354.
5. No product code is changed.

## Who it is for

William (GitHub `swill-ib`).

How to run it:
- Use the same method as Part 3 (`git clone --no-local --depth 1`, then `codegraph init --yes <clone>`, peak memory from `resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss` taken after the build exits, `codegraph status` after init has exited).
- Stop raising N if available memory falls below about 4 GiB, and say so in the report.
- Run it in a fresh test workspace, not your everyday one, as in the Part 3 setup.
- Clay's decision: the 2,000-token overage and the `init-lite --dry-run` exit code are accepted and need no work from this issue.

# Concurrent codegraph indexing report

## Test scope and purpose

The tests measured memory use and completion time when multiple first-time codegraph indexes run concurrently on a single workspace. They address [issue 648](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/648), which extends earlier single-build measurements to assess resource pressure when several fresh repository checkouts start indexing at once.

Each repository was tested separately with 1, 3, 5 and 10 simultaneous builds. Every build used a fresh shallow clone of the same recorded commit, producing eight test batches and 38 index builds. Only codegraph indexing was measured; the applications contained in the repositories were not run.

| Repository | Description | Commit tested |
|---|---|---|
| [PrivateProjectA](https://github.com/PrivateOrg/PrivateProjectA) | private project A repository | `<private-project-commit>` |
| [IronClaude](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude) | Engineering workflow framework for Claude Code | `1a6c8723fe9e6caa85bfffcdb97b2dc434978bf9` |

The recorded measurements were each build's peak memory and elapsed time, the highest memory usage of each simultaneously indexed repository copy added together, and the workspace's lowest sampled available memory. Total workspace memory and build completion status were also recorded to establish the test conditions and identify failures.

---

## Findings

### Method

Fresh shallow clones were created with `git clone --no-local --depth 1` from the existing local checkouts. Every clone was checked against its repository's recorded commit and confirmed to have no existing codegraph index. Source commits: PrivateProjectA `<private-project-commit>`; IronClaude `1a6c8723fe9e6caa85bfffcdb97b2dc434978bf9`. Local clones exclude uncommitted files and are not a fetch of the remote's latest branch.

Each indexing command, `codegraph init --yes <clone>`, was launched by a separate Python measuring process. After the command finished, its peak memory was read using `resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss`. The tested codegraph version was 1.6.2. Elapsed time was measured with a monotonic clock from command launch to completion; it includes process startup and polling overhead, but excludes cloning and subsequent status checks. On Linux the peak is in KiB. Adding the highest memory usage from each simultaneously indexed copy does not measure their combined memory usage at a single instant.

A separate measuring process was prepared for each index build. All measuring processes waited for the same start signal, then launched their builds together so the batch tested concurrent indexing rather than a sequence of separate runs. Available and total workspace memory were recorded every 0.5 seconds until the builds finished; the reported minimum also includes the immediate pre-launch reading.

A test is not started if available memory is below 4 GiB. If available memory falls below 4 GiB, the running test is stopped and tests with more simultaneous builds are not attempted. A 900-second batch timeout also preserves stopped outcomes. Index status was checked only after all indexing commands finished and no init/index/sync process was detected. Each repository and simultaneous-build count was tested once, not in repeated trials.

### Batch summary

All 38 init commands exited 0, and all 38 post-init statuses report index state `complete`. Every requested level ran: none was skipped, killed, failed or stopped. Each PrivateProjectA index has 1,091 files; each IronClaude index has 3,519 files.
All memory columns below are **KiB**. The elapsed-time range shows the fastest and slowest build in each group. Workspace total is the observed `MemTotal` range during that batch, not an assumed fixed hardware capacity. The individual-build sections below provide the measurements behind each batch's peak-memory sum and elapsed-time range.

| Repository | Simultaneous builds | Sum of individual peaks (KiB) | Per-build elapsed range (s) | Lowest sampled available (KiB) | Observed total memory range (KiB) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PrivateProjectA | 1 | 1,558,724 | 26.539-26.539 | 60,260,844 | 91,198,104-91,505,304 |
| PrivateProjectA | 3 | 4,453,372 | 27.486-27.564 | 60,508,452 | 90,276,504-90,583,704 |
| PrivateProjectA | 5 | 7,609,324 | 29.160-29.539 | 58,468,752 | 89,047,704-89,354,904 |
| PrivateProjectA | 10 | 14,731,744 | 33.686-34.765 | 51,906,068 | 87,818,904-88,126,104 |
| IronClaude | 1 | 3,981,696 | 38.282-38.282 | 61,755,640 | 88,126,104-88,433,304 |
| IronClaude | 3 | 11,501,152 | 41.174-41.377 | 55,078,324 | 88,740,504-89,047,704 |
| IronClaude | 5 | 18,953,840 | 47.613-47.975 | 48,200,940 | 88,433,304-88,842,904 |
| IronClaude | 10 | 40,213,880 | 74.409-77.585 | 25,684,312 | 88,620,168-89,336,968 |

### Measurement validation

The measurement script passed nine regression checks. Independent review confirmed that memory readings covered every build from start to finish and satisfied the required sampling interval of one second or less; the longest observed gap was 0.524 seconds. Builds within each batch started within 4 milliseconds of one another.
### Individual builds: PrivateProjectA

Each row reports one index build's peak memory and elapsed time, with elapsed time rounded to 0.001 seconds.

| Simultaneous builds | Build within batch | Peak memory (KiB) | Elapsed (s) | Exit code |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 1,558,724 | 26.539 | 0 |
| 3 | 1 | 1,442,764 | 27.564 | 0 |
| 3 | 2 | 1,506,412 | 27.504 | 0 |
| 3 | 3 | 1,504,196 | 27.486 | 0 |
| 5 | 1 | 1,540,996 | 29.539 | 0 |

| 5 | 4 | 1,536,852 | 29.346 | 0 |
| 5 | 5 | 1,539,432 | 29.414 | 0 |

| 10 | 10 | 1,481,432 | 34.350 | 0 |

### Individual builds: IronClaude

These rows use the same per-build measurements and rounding as the PrivateProjectA results.

| Simultaneous builds | Build within batch | Peak memory (KiB) | Elapsed (s) | Exit code |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 3,981,696 | 38.282 | 0 |
| 3 | 1 | 3,863,424 | 41.377 | 0 |
| 3 | 2 | 3,817,692 | 41.174 | 0 |
| 3 | 3 | 3,820,036 | 41.292 | 0 |
| 5 | 1 | 3,842,524 | 47.975 | 0 |
| 5 | 2 | 3,772,828 | 47.613 | 0 |
| 5 | 3 | 3,744,572 | 47.846 | 0 |
| 5 | 4 | 3,781,056 | 47.673 | 0 |
| 5 | 5 | 3,812,860 | 47.811 | 0 |
| 10 | 1 | 3,909,644 | 74.409 | 0 |
| 10 | 2 | 4,091,848 | 75.286 | 0 |
| 10 | 3 | 4,172,508 | 76.245 | 0 |
| 10 | 4 | 4,150,664 | 77.408 | 0 |
| 10 | 5 | 3,934,960 | 74.858 | 0 |
| 10 | 6 | 3,936,444 | 76.658 | 0 |
| 10 | 7 | 3,863,736 | 76.612 | 0 |
| 10 | 8 | 4,126,040 | 77.585 | 0 |
| 10 | 9 | 4,019,588 | 77.172 | 0 |
| 10 | 10 | 4,008,448 | 77.245 | 0 |

### Observations

Measured windows ran on 2026-11-20 from 21:27:42 UTC to 21:42:13 UTC, on Linux `6.8.0-149-generic`, with 28 logical CPUs reported and Python 3.13.5. During measured batches the kernel-visible total memory varied from 87,818,904 to 91,505,304 KiB (about 83.75-87.27 GiB).

All 38 indexes completed with no build failure, signal kill, safety stop or timeout. None of the sampled available-memory values crossed below 4 GiB. The lowest observed available memory was 25,684,312 KiB (24.494 GiB) in the ten-build IronClaude batch. The operating-system counters checked before and after each test recorded no new out-of-memory events or memory-related process kills.

The ten-build PrivateProjectA sum of individual peaks was 14,731,744 KiB (14.049 GiB). The ten-build IronClaude sum was 40,213,880 KiB (38.351 GiB). Across all counts, individual PrivateProjectA peaks were 1,441,340-1,558,724 KiB (1.375-1.487 GiB), and individual IronClaude peaks were 3,744,572-4,172,508 KiB (3.571-3.979 GiB). All individual peaks exceeded the earlier 1,048,576 KiB per-build budget quoted in issue 648.

Observable slowdown: the median per-build elapsed time at ten simultaneous builds was 34.301 s for PrivateProjectA versus 26.539 s alone (1.29 times), and 76.635 s for IronClaude versus 38.282 s alone (2.00 times). The largest measured sampling gap remained 0.524 s after rounding, so the one-second sampling requirement was met despite slower builds.

No product source code was changed during the tests.

## Gaps

- Individual readings may fluctuate with normal system activity.
- Each simultaneously indexed repository copy contributes its highest memory reading to the reported sum. Those highs may occur at different times, so the sum does not show how much memory all builds used together at one moment.
- One batch per repository/count, not replicated trials. Local shallow clones and existing filesystem caches mean first index, not guaranteed cold filesystem cache. No causal claim is made that every system-wide memory change was due solely to codegraph.
- `MemTotal` changed during and between batches; these are kernel-visible values in this workspace, not proof of a fixed physical-machine capacity.
- Source snapshots differ from the earlier issue's IronClaude `3f3b34a2` quick check. This is not an exact repeat of that snapshot, and no between-snapshot regression conclusion is claimed.
- User-perceived machine slowness was not separately tested. All raw index commands exited 0, statuses were complete, and observed timing/sampling evidence is supplied instead.
- Independent review of the collected measurements and reported results was completed successfully. A cancellation-safety defect in the measuring script was corrected and rechecked before any index test ran.

## Key Takeaways

The requested local 1/3/5/10-build matrix ran for both repositories, 38 first indexes total, without crossing the 4 GiB available-memory stop threshold. Ten IronClaude builds produced a 38.351 GiB sum of individual peaks and roughly doubled median build time on this workspace; the lowest sampled available memory remained 24.494 GiB. These measurements do not show compliance with the earlier 1 GiB per-build budget.

title: Measure codegraph first-index memory when several builds run at the same time on one workspace
